narration.text: Massive money for AI chips, and Claude is going mobile. Let's get into it.
TechCrunch reports that AI chip maker SambaNova has raised 1 billion dollars. This puts their valuation at 11 billion pounds. It comes just months after their last mega-round.
Anthropic's Claude Cowork platform is now available on mobile and web. TechCrunch reports this expanded access starts for Max subscribers. It will roll out to other Claude users in coming weeks.
Hot French startup ZML has released free software, ZML/LLMD. TechCrunch states this product could make running AI less costly. It is designed to speed inference across many AI chips.
Ars Technica reports that hackers can use nine popular AI tools. This allows them to assemble massive botnets. It weaponises large language models' inability to say 'I don't know'.
That's your AI news for today. Which story do you think is most important? Let us know in the comments. And follow for tomorrow's AI news brief.

description: Catch up on today's top AI headlines. We cover SambaNova's huge new funding round, Anthropic's Claude Cowork expanding to mobile, and a new free tool from ZML to speed up AI chips. Plus, we look at how hackers are exploiting popular AI tools.
